title: DTC tokenization service on Stellar: inferred and unknown rows
description: Stellar-specific rows layered on dtc-generic. DTCC has NOT published Stellar requirements (gate G-DTCC). Every row here is inferred or unknown. When DTCC publishes, change this data file and re-run conformance; code does not change.
disclaimer: DTC-shaped, not DTC-certified. Every Stellar row in this profile is inferred or unknown: DTCC has published no Stellar wallet, token or API requirements. Do not describe any output built on these rows as DTC-compatible.

rows.statement: DTCC's product page lists Stellar (SEP-41) as anticipated in 2027 (the dtcc.com launch release does not name Stellar).

sources.title: DTCC tokenization product page, per-network tiles

rows.basis: The statement is on a marketing-tier product page and in a brochure PDF. It is not a requirement, a participant guide or a dated commitment, and DTCC's NAL says the approved-protocol list will be published separately. Kept inferred under G-DTCC.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC list of supported tokenization protocols/ledgers; Stellar tile moving from 'soon' to live

rows.statement: The token interface on Stellar is SEP-41 (transfer, balance, allowance, burn). SEP-41 has no allowlist, freeze or forced transfer; the Stellar Asset Contract implements SEP-41 and SEP-57 extends it.

sources.title: SEP-41 Soroban Token Interface, Draft v0.5.2 updated 2026-08-24

rows.basis: Names an interface, not a compliance mechanism. The SEP is still Draft, so the tile may change when it revises.

rows.statement: Which concrete token form DTCC will use on Stellar: classic asset fronted by a SAC, an OpenZeppelin SEP-57 (T-REX) contract token, or a bespoke contract minted by DTC's tokenization engine.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC Stellar participant/wallet guide or supported-protocols list

rows.statement: How 'transferable only to Registered Wallets' is enforced on Stellar. Candidates: classic AUTH_REQUIRED with DTC authorising each trustline (SetTrustLineFlags); SEP-57 identity verifier plus compliance modules; SEP-8 approval server per payment. The compliance mechanism is undecided in public.
If the classic-asset form is used, registering a wallet takes two steps: the participant creates a trustline, then DTC authorises it. Until authorised the wallet cannot receive.

sources.title: SDF docs: control asset access (mirror read in discovery)

rows.basis: Follows from how AUTH_REQUIRED works on classic assets (holder must open the trustline, issuer flips the authorised flag). Applies only if DTCC chooses the classic form.

rows.statement: Classic assets and the SAC have 7 fixed decimals, so 'no fractional tokens' cannot be enforced by asset flags; a contract token with decimals 0 can enforce it. This favours a contract token.

sources.title: DTCC tokenization product page
sources.locator: SEP-41 tile only; whole-token rule is token.whole-tokens-only

rows.basis: Stellar protocol knowledge (SAC amounts are i128 with 7 decimals), not re-verified against docs at scaffold time. Ticket DTC-024 tests it on testnet.
rows.unblockedBy: Testnet spike DTC-024 and DTCC choice of token form

rows.statement: Which Stellar address kinds can be a Registered Wallet: G-account, C-contract address, muxed M-address, smart account. DTC does not validate addresses, so any can be typed in; whether DTC's tokenization engine can mint to them is unknown.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC Stellar Wallet Solution Provider Connectivity Guide

rows.statement: Open question: can a contract (C...) address be a Registered Wallet? It decides whether a DvP escrow or smart account can ever hold DTC tokens. Note a classic payment operation cannot have a contract address as source or destination; SAC transfers to a C-address need the contract to be authorised first under AUTH_REQUIRED.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC Stellar Wallet Solution Provider Connectivity Guide, or an answer from DTCC via SDF's enterprise team (user outreach, G-OUTREACH)

rows.statement: How the DTC root override is realised on Stellar. Classic: clawback is a burn, so a force transfer is a clawback plus an issuer payment in one transaction. SEP-57: forced_transfer / recover_balance. SAC: mint, clawback, set_authorized.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC token-form decision; whether DTC accepts clawback+payment as 'transaction reversibility'

rows.statement: Who holds DTC's 'root wallet' key on Stellar: the classic issuer account, a SAC admin contract, or a SEP-57 operator role, and whether it is multi-signature.

How chill/lock states map to Stellar: classic AUTH_REVOCABLE (revoke authorisation) or AUTHORIZED_TO_MAINTAIN_LIABILITIES; SEP-57 set_address_frozen / freeze_partial_tokens / pause; or a DTCC-side status only with no on-chain effect.
Token events a participant decodes: SEP-41 / CAP-67 transfer, mint, burn, approve topics (optional muxed fields); SEP-57 adds recovery_success, address-frozen, tokens-frozen events.
rows.basis: Standard event layouts are public; whether DTC's admin actions look like normal transfers or distinct events is unknown (events.admin-action-visibility).

rows.statement: Whether a DTC force transfer, clawback or mint is distinguishable on-chain from an ordinary participant transfer, and how LedgerScan's Stellar scanner and retention window work.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC LedgerScan Stellar scanner documentation (not public)

rows.statement: Confirmation threshold at which DTCC marks a conversion order Completed on Stellar.
Who pays Stellar fees and reserves: the participant, DTC for mint transactions, or a sponsor (sponsored reserves, fee-bump).

How a CUSIP maps to a Stellar asset (asset code + issuer, or contract ID) and which stellar.toml / SEP-1 data is expected. The DTCC Eligible Securities screen lists token and wallet address per chain, so the mapping is DTC-side data.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC Eligible Securities data for Stellar

rows.statement: Whether DTCC will certify wallet providers on Stellar, the connectivity handshake in the Wallet Solution Provider Connectivity Guide, and the signature scheme its registry expects.
rows.unblockedBy: DTCC Wallet Solution Provider Connectivity Guide (login-gated); a DTCC relationship via SDF or a listed wallet provider

rows.statement: An issuer-run SEP-8 approval server gates each payment at the issuer. For DTC tokens the issuer role is DTC's tokenization engine, which mints and configures tokens; participants do not run approval servers. Fit is judged poor: SEP-8 is Active but last updated 2022, only SDF's demo wallet has client support in the SDF repos checked, and custody stacks (raw-XDR signing) have no evidenced SEP-8 flow.

sources.title: SEP-8 Regulated Assets, Active v1.7.4 updated 2022-02-21

rows.basis: Judgement from institutional_tooling_gaps.md (client support check was file-path based, weak) and from the NAL statement that DTC, not participants, configures tokens. See readiness-pack/sep8-and-contract-wallets.md.
